title: People Ops — Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide (2026)
author: Sophie Clarke
body:
Purpose
-------
This guide documents Redwood Inference’s standard processes and manager responsibilities for hiring, employee onboarding, and the performance & feedback cycle. It consolidates the operational steps, templates, SLAs, and decision points people managers and interviewers must follow so we hire consistently, onboard efficiently, and run fair, calibrated performance reviews.

Scope
-----
Applies to: all hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and engineering managers. Excludes: contractor or vendor procurement (see finance-and-legal).

Owner and SLAs
--------------
- Owner: People Ops (primary)
- Support: Hiring managers, Recruiting, Legal (offers/agreements)
- Typical SLA: Requisition approval <= 3 business days; Offer approval <= 24 hours after comp sign-off; New hire first-day readiness >= 100% by 9am local time.

1) Hiring process (end-to-end)
-----------------------------
Summary: requisition -> sourcing -> interviewing -> decision -> offer -> background & onboarding.

Step-by-step
1. Requisition & role spec (Hiring manager)
   - Create/approve requisition in Lever (or HRIS). Attach updated role profile and scorecard.
   - Required fields: team, level, hiring rationale, expected timeline, compensation band (from People Ops).
2. Intake with Recruiting (30–60 min)
   - Align on must-have vs nice-to-have skills, interviewers, diversity goals, and target timeline.
3. Sourcing & screening (Recruiting)
   - Recruiter performs initial phone screen using 6-question screen template.
4. Interview loop (hiring team + cross-functional)
   - Typical loop: 1) Technical screen (45 min) 2) Deep technical (pairing or take-home) 3) System design / architecture 4) Collaboration and values interview 5) Hiring manager final
   - Use scorecard (see table below) and collect written feedback within 24 hours.
5. Decision & calibration (Manager + Panel)
   - Manager convenes panel (asynchronous ok) to reach consensus within 48 hours of final interview. If disagreement, escalate to Director for tie-break.
6. Offer (People Ops + Legal)
   - People Ops drafts offer within 24 hours of decision. Manager reviews, then recruiter extends. Use standard offer template.
7. Background & verification (Ops)
   - Complete background check and I-9 (where applicable) before start date.
8. Decline & debrief
   - Send thoughtful decline note. Offer feedback on request (no benchmarks or salary details).

Interview scorecard (one-line summary per dimension)
| Dimension | Rating 1–5 | Guidance |
|---|---:|---|
| Role competence (core skills) |  | Does candidate demonstrate the minimum technical/product skills required? |
| Problem solving & design |  | Clarity of thought, tradeoffs, system thinking |
| Execution & past impact |  | Evidence of shipping and measurable impact |
| Collaboration & communication |  | Cross-team work, clarity, feedback receptivity |
| Learning & growth mindset |  | Openness to feedback and fast learning |
| Cultural fit & values |  | Alignment with Redwood’s principles (ownership, empathy, rigor) |
| Overall hire/bench |  | Recommended level and confidence (hire/no-hire) |

Interviewer guidelines and bias mitigation
- Require a concrete score and 2–3 bullet examples per interview. Avoid phrasing like "seems smart."
- Use structured questions mapped to scorecard dimensions.
- Interview panel must include at least one interviewer trained in inclusive interviewing for senior roles.
- Do not ask questions about protected characteristics. For immigration-related queries, consult Recruiting or Legal.

2) Onboarding (first 90 days)
----------------------------
Principles: reduce time-to-productivity, signal belonging, and set clear success metrics.

Pre-Start (Owner: Recruiting + IT + Hiring manager)
- Equipment ordered and delivered (laptop, monitors) at least 3 business days before start.
- Accounts provisioned: Google Workspace, Slack, Redwood Console (read-only first), HRIS, JIRA.
- First-week schedule shared: 1:1s, orientation, team welcome.

First day checklist (Manager + People Ops)
| Item | Owner | Target completion |
|---|---|---|
| Welcome & orientation session (30–60m) | People Ops | Day 1 AM |
| Manager 1:1 (role & expectations) | Hiring manager | Day 1 PM |
| Team lunch / intro | Team | Day 1 |
| Equipment and account verification | IT | Day 1 |
| Security & compliance training | Security | Day 1–3 |

First week
- Assign onboarding buddy.
- Deliver a 30–60–90 plan draft with measurable goals (see template link).
- Small, meaningful first task shipped (docs/bug/feature).

30–60–90 example milestones
- 30 days: complete core trainings, join product/infra walkthroughs, ship small bugfix.
- 60 days: own a small feature/ops task end-to-end, present learnings.
- 90 days: operate independently on team standard tasks, set performance goals for review.

Ongoing onboarding (first 6 months)
- Weekly manager check-ins for first 3 months, then bi-weekly.
- People Ops touchpoints at week 2 and month 3 for calibration.

3) Performance & feedback cycle
--------------------------------
Cadence
- Quarterly check-ins: informal 30-minute touchpoints to track progress and remove blockers.
- Mid-year review: formative, focuses on development and course-correction.
- Annual review: summative, compensation and promotion decisions.

Process (Manager responsibilities)
1. Set clear goals within first 30 days (SMART-aligned).
2. Run monthly feedback conversations (documented in manager notes).
3. Prepare for calibration: collect evidence (projects, PRs, feedback) and submit to People Ops by the schedule.
4. Complete written reviews in the HRIS by the deadline.

Calibration & rating guidelines
- Calibration is team-level plus cross-team director review to ensure fairness.
- Use evidence-based ratings (not personality). Ratings map to compensation bands and promotion eligibility.

Promotion & leveling
- Promotion requires demonstrated impact at the next level’s expectations over a sustained period (typically 6–12 months).
- Managers must provide concrete examples mapped to the leveling rubric and assemble a promotion packet (work samples, endorsements). People Ops coordinates the committee.

Managed performance and improvement plans (PIP)
- When performance is below expectations after coaching, managers may initiate a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) with People Ops. PIPs are 30–90 days, with clear success criteria and weekly check-ins. Legal is consulted for final steps.

4) Manager playbook (practical checklist)
----------------------------------------
Hiring
- Write a clear role brief and scorecard.
- Interview with a standard rubric and provide timely feedback.

Onboarding
- Draft 30–60–90 plan and schedule recurring 1:1s.
- Introduce buddy and set first deliverable.

Performance
- Document expectations, run regular check-ins, keep records of successes and concerns.
- Prepare evidence for calibration and promotion cycles.

People Care & Retention
- Run stay conversations at 3 and 6 months.
- Escalate retention risks to People Ops for role adjustments or comp market checks.

Templates and reference links
- Role scorecard template: /confluence/templates/role-scorecard (internal)
- Offer template: /confluence/templates/offer-letter-standard
- 30–60–90 plan template: /confluence/templates/30-60-90

Compliance and privacy notes
- All interview notes and candidate data must be stored in Lever and treated as confidential.
- Background checks require candidate consent and are retained per data-retention policy (see security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention).

Ownership & escalation
- People Ops: process owner for hiring, offers, and onboarding design.
- Hiring manager: primary owner for candidate decision, onboarding success, and performance management.
- Recruiting: source and screen candidates, coordinate interview logistics.
- Escalation path: Manager -> Director -> VP People -> Legal (for compliance/offer disputes).

Metrics and success signals
- Time-to-offer median <= 21 days.
- First-90 retention >= 90% for engineering hires.
- New-hire time-to-productivity (manager-assessed) median <= 8 weeks.

Frequently asked questions
Q: What if a candidate declines an offer?
A: Debrief on why; if compensation is the blocker, consult People Ops for a counteroffer decision. Maintain transparent timing expectations for the team.

Q: Can managers make exceptions to the interview loop?
A: Minor exceptions require Recruiting sign-off; major deviations (e.g., skip technical loop) require Director approval.

Q: How do we handle remote hires across time zones?
A: Coordinate start-of-day orientation by timezone and stagger welcome sessions; ensure equipment and accounts are ready in the local region prior to start.
